content.text: Section 22 fully meets the preferred position, and Section 23 contains only a heading with no substantive audit or records obligation on us.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 already matches our preferred position in every parameter: audits of Customer usage are limited to once in any twelve-month period (22.1), require thirty days' prior written notice, must occur during normal business hours without unreasonable disruption, must be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1), and Vendor bears audit costs unless an underpayment exceeding five percent is established (22.2). Section 22.2 also expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, and other suppliers' confidential information, so the walk-away risks (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote system access) are absent. Section 22.3 adds Customer-favourable protections (findings are Customer Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of the final report, and finality on payment of a shortfall). Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains only a heading with no operative text, and a full-text search for audit/inspection/verification/records language found no other provision creating an audit or inspection right against Customer. No redline is needed.
